title: LedgerMath data API, version 1: the list of Series
description: v1/series.json: one row per Series, each with the address of its own file, and each Method's own words for what its numbers mean. A Series is the Runs of one benchmark, parameter set (params), build, instance type and Availability Zone ID. A versioned Method turns a Series' Runs into a Derivation; a row holds a summary of each Method's Derivation of the Series under derivations, keyed <method name>_v<version>, and the Series' file holds them in full. The row's figures are the Derivations' own, at the same paths, with the bulky parts (lists of Runs, histograms) left to the Series' file; nothing is rounded. Each row is written on one line of its own. Version 1 only ever gains fields: a field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know, which is why no object in this schema forbids members it does not list. A new Method, or a new version of one, is a new key beside the old ones. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1.

schema.description: What this file is, and which version of its shape.

index.description: The address of the table of contents, v1/index.json.

newest_run_started_at.description: When the newest Run of any Series started; null when there is no Series.

methods.description: Each Method's own words, from its file of Derivations, keyed <method name>_v<version>: how each number is made, what splits a Series into groups, and the Run files it read and could not read. A Run file that does not validate against the Run schema is in no Series; it is listed here, under unreadable, with why and the address of the file.

series_v1.description: Method series, version 1: every Series; one number per Run, and the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles across Runs.

split_on.description: The facts a Series is split into groups on, in order.

left_out.description: What is left out of a dump section before it is compared for the split, and why.

not_split_on.description: Facts the Runs record that do not split a Series, and why.

sections.description: How often each dump section's hash changed, over every Run read: the evidence for the split facts. Counts of Runs and of pairs of consecutive Runs.

runs.description: Runs whose dumps hold the section.

changed_within_run.description: Of those, the Runs whose before-dump and after-dump hold different hashes for it.

boot_pairs.description: Pairs of consecutive Runs of one boot, whatever their Series.

changed_within_boot.description: Of those, the pairs whose before-dumps hold different hashes for it.

series_pairs.description: Pairs of consecutive Runs of one Series, summed over every Series.

changed_between_runs.description: Of those, the pairs whose before-dumps hold different hashes for it.

split_on.description: The split fact read from the section, or null.

requests_v1.description: Method requests, version 1: the Series whose samples are requests; each phase of a request, across the requests, within each Run and pooled across Runs.

phases.description: The phases of a request, each an interval between two of its events, in nanoseconds of the Run's clock.

percentiles.description: The percentiles reported, and the fewest requests that support each.

request_facts.description: The facts each request records of its connection or of itself.

split_on.description: Method series v1's split facts, which give the same groups.

runs_read.description: Run files read, of every kind.

series.description: One row per Series, in the order benchmark, instance type, zone ID, params, build.

time.description: UTC, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it.

definitions.description: How each number is made, in the Method's words, by name.

section.description: The dump section it is read from, if it is.

unreadable.description: A Run file the Method could not read: it does not validate against the Run schema, so it is in no Series.

path.description: The Run file's path in the Runs repository.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the Run file's bytes, in hex.

least_requests.description: The fewest requests that support it: at least one request is then expected above it.

precision.description: A pooled percentile is within this fraction of the exact percentile of the same requests.

params.description: The parameter set, as each Run was given it (LM_PARAM_*).

stat_summary.description: Percentiles of one number across the Series' counted Runs. The Series' file lists the Runs behind them.

request_stats.description: One phase over a set of requests, in nanoseconds: the count of requests, the least and greatest time, and each percentile the count supports (null when it does not), with how many requests are ranked at or above each one reported.

phase_stats.description: Each phase's statistics, by phase; a phase no request had is absent (dns, connect and tls over a kept connection).

id.description: The Series' id: the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of its key (benchmark, params, build, instance type, zone ID) as canonical JSON.

url.description: The address of the Series' own file, v1/series/<id>.json.

build.description: The named build of the benchmark (static, dynamic).

instance_type.description: The EC2 instance type, as the provider names it.

availability_zone_id.description: The Availability Zone ID, as the provider names it.

runs.description: Runs in the Series, counted or not.

newest_run_started_at.description: When its newest Run started: the moment a citation of the Series as it stands names.

derivations.description: A summary of each Method's Derivation of the Series, keyed <method name>_v<version>. Method series v1 derives every Series; Method requests v1 only those whose samples are requests, and its key is absent from the others.

failed_runs.description: Runs it does not count: shown in the Series' file with why, in no percentile.

groups.description: How many groups its split facts make of the Series' Runs.

percentiles.description: Across every counted Run of the Series, whatever its group. Null when no Run counts, or for bytes_per_second when the benchmark observes no bytes per repetition.

time_per_repetition_ns.description: Nanoseconds per repetition: each Run's median over its counted samples.

bytes_per_second.description: Bytes per second: each Run's bytes per repetition × 10^9 / its time per repetition in nanoseconds.

counted_runs.description: Runs this Method counts (exit 0, or 4 with failed requests).

pool.description: Every succeeded request of the Series' counted Runs, pooled: each phase's statistics, read from the summed histogram (the Series' file holds the histograms, and the breakdowns by request fact).
